title: Unramifiedness from ordinary fibres
statement: Let $h:Z\to B$ be a morphism of schemes locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. For every point $s\in B$, let $Z_s=Z\times_B\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ be the scheme-theoretic fibre [def-pc-scheme-fibre], where $\kappa(s)$ is the residue field [def-weil-residue-field]. If each $Z_s\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ is a disjoint union of spectra [def-weil-affine-spectrum] of finite separable algebraic field extensions [def-pc-field-extension] [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension] of $\kappa(s)$, then $h$ is unramified [def-weil-unramified-morphism].

proof.text: For every $s\in B$, the assumed disjoint-union description and [lem-trf-unramified-field-fibre-decomposition] give that $Z_s\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ is unramified. Apply [lem-trf-unramified-fibres-affine-differentials] to $h$: over each affine target open $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$ it gives a covering by $U_i=\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ with $A_i$ finitely generated over $R$, and for every prime $\mathfrak p\subset R$ it gives $\Omega_{(A_i\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p))/\kappa(\mathfrak p)}=0$. These covers, as $V$ varies, cover $Z$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 02G8(2), affine-chart reduction, using Lemma Tag 02G7(1) (lemma-unramified-over-field)

proof.text: For each chart $R\to A_i$ from step 1, apply [lem-trf-fibrewise-zero-kahler-differentials]. Its finite-generation and fibre-differential hypotheses are precisely the conclusions of step 1, so $\Omega_{A_i/R}=0$. The affine criterion [lem-weil-pbc-unramified-ring-map-iff-unramified-affine] now shows that $U_i\to V$ is unramified, since $A_i$ is finitely generated over $R$ and its relative differentials vanish.

source.place: Lemma Tag 02G8(2); the algebraic argument is Algebra Lemma Tag 00UV(7)--(9),(11), and the affine criterion is Lemma Tag 02G6

proof.text: The charts of step 1 cover $Z$, and step 2 makes their maps to the respective target affine opens unramified. Thus $h$ has an affine covering with finite-type ring maps and zero relative differentials. This is exactly the affine-cover characterization explicitly included in [def-weil-unramified-morphism]; hence $h$ is unramified.

lean.statement: theorem unramified_of_ordinary_fibre_coproduct_finite_separable {Z B : Scheme.{u}} (h : Z ⟶ B) [LocallyOfFiniteType h] : (∀ s : B, ∃ (I : Type u) (L : I → Type u) (hfield : ∀ i, Field (L i)) (halg : ∀ i, Algebra (B.residueField s) (L i)), (∀ i, @Module.Finite (B.residueField s) (L i) inferInstance (hfield i).toCommRing.toRing.toAddCommGroup.toAddCommMonoid (halg i).toModule) ∧ (∀ i, @Algebra.IsSeparable (B.residueField s) (L i) inferInstance (hfield i).toCommRing.toRing (halg i)) ∧ ∃ e : h.fiber s ≅ ∐ (fun i : I ↦ Spec (CommRingCat.of (L i))), e.hom ≫ Sigma.desc (fun i : I ↦ (Spec.homEquiv (R := B.residueField s) (S := CommRingCat.of (L i))).symm (CommRingCat.ofHom (@algebraMap (B.residueField s) (L i) inferInstance (hfield i).toCommRing.toSemiring (halg i)))) = h.fiberToSpecResidueField s) → LocallyOfFiniteType h ∧ IsOpenImmersion (pullback.diagonal h)
